assessor: RTS implementation preflight — Adaptive Intelligence v2
rationale: The parent candidate now has enough evidence to define its architecture, but it spans five independently risky implementation grounds with different storage, routing, checkpoint, telemetry, and provenance boundaries. A monolithic PR would make rollback, validation, and causal attribution worse. The parent should remain FROZEN and be decomposed into five children, each separately assessed and approved under WIP=1.
affected_boundaries: FREEZER parent architecture and future child candidates
always-loaded instruction surface and restart state
existing Outcome Learning / Skill Regression / Human Review / Promotion Preview integration
existing_assumptions: Existing RTS governance components remain authoritative and must not be duplicated.
Memory retrieval is advisory context and never grants execution or promotion authority.
Raw outcome/evidence can be persisted independently from later intelligence compilation.
Each child can be implemented behind a bounded repository-local interface before any cross-repo or provider automation is considered.
WIP=1 and explicit human build authority remain mandatory for active child work.

data_migration.notes: The parent decomposition itself requires no data migration. Any child that introduces a durable memory or checkpoint schema must define its own migration/compatibility boundary in its own Preflight.

external_interfaces: GitHub repositories and exact public source refs used only as governed evidence/reuse inputs
optional provider-side token/cache telemetry as a read-only metric source when available
no provider/network execution is authorized by the parent
no external repository writes are authorized by the parent
approval_changes: No existing approval authority is widened.
The parent remains NOT_APPROVED and FROZEN.
Each child must receive its own current Build Assessment, PASS Preflight, and explicit human approval before SELECTED/IN_PROGRESS.
Canonical memory or Skill promotion continues to require existing Human Review / regression / Promotion Preview boundaries.
public_documents: Draft PR #365 and its bounded assessment inputs
regression_tests: Parent decomposition must not alter current governed-loop outputs or authority.
Existing FREEZER verification and WIP=1 constraints must remain unchanged.
Existing Outcome Learning, Skill Regression, Human Review Ledger, Promotion Preview, and governed-loop tests remain green after each child.
Each child must prove deterministic behavior or explicitly bounded non-determinism at its own owner boundary.
No child may convert retrieved memory, external evidence, or cache telemetry into execution authority.
hidden_dependencies: manifest and index rebuilding after FREEZER mutations
exact source identity for external references
future storage owner for reusable intelligence records
future restart-item register and equivalence criteria
future checkpoint identity and idempotency rules
availability and semantics of provider cache telemetry
rollback_boundary: The parent decomposition is documentation/FREEZER metadata only. Before any child implementation, rollback is deletion/reversion of newly created child candidate records and restoration of the prior parent current pointer/index/manifest state. No runtime behavior, Skill, external repository, or provider state is changed by decomposition.
completion_conditions: RTS-FRZ-000001 is revised to the v2 parent architecture while remaining FROZEN / NOT_APPROVED.
A current Build Assessment records exact reuse sources, license boundaries, gaps, and parent-level cost/value.
A current Preflight records DECOMPOSE_REQUIRED and names all five children.
Five child FREEZER candidates are created as FROZEN / NOT_APPROVED with no implementation side effects.
FREEZER indexes and manifest verify after decomposition.
The next active implementation, if any, is one separately assessed and human-approved child under WIP=1.

child_candidates: Reuse Efficiency + Knowledge Debt Metrics v1
External Transition Pattern Seed Corpus v1

risks: Creating all children may be mistaken for approval to build all children.
A child may duplicate an existing RTS governance owner unless its Preflight checks ownership first.
Cross-child schema coupling could recreate a monolith if shared contracts are not kept minimal.
Telemetry work may drift into unsupported claims about OpenAI quota/cache causality.
External pattern corpus work may drift into code copying or canonical promotion without evidence.
